title: AbbVie partners with Germany’s Disco Pharmaceuticals in US$2.5B cancer drug discovery deal
summary: The partnership will use Disco’s DiscoTech platform, which maps proteins expressed on the surface of cancer cells, collectively known as the surfaceome.

contentHtml:
GERMANY—AbbVie has entered an option-to-license agreement with Disco Pharmaceuticals, committing up to US$2.5 billion to discover and develop cancer-targeted bispecific antibodies for patients with solid tumours.

The agreement includes a US$40 million upfront payment, with additional funding tied to research, development and commercial milestones.

The collaboration will focus on identifying highly selective targets and potentially advancing new bispecific therapies designed to distinguish cancer cells from healthy tissue.

Platform targets cancer cell surface proteins

The partnership will use Disco’s DiscoTech platform, which maps proteins expressed on the surface of cancer cells, collectively known as the surfaceome.

This approach helps identify potential targets for AND-gated bispecific antibodies, which are designed to recognise two molecular markers before activating their therapeutic effects.

Unlike conventional antibodies that may recognise a single target, AND-gated approaches aim to improve tumour selectivity by requiring the presence of multiple markers.

This could help reduce damage to healthy tissue, particularly in solid tumours where identifying cancer-specific targets remains a challenge.

Disco CEO Mark Manfredi said the collaboration provides an opportunity to develop precision medicines for patients with difficult-to-treat solid tumours.

He noted that the company’s AND-gated technology is designed to selectively target cancer cells while sparing healthy tissue.

Manfredi assumed the chief executive role in December 2025.

AbbVie expands its bispecific antibody pipeline

Founded in 2022, Disco emerged from research conducted at Switzerland’s ETH Zürich.

Roman Thomas, a professor of translational genomics at the University of Cologne, initially led the company as CEO. Dieter Weinand, former CEO of Bayer, serves as chairman of its board.

AbbVie had established an early relationship with Disco through its venture capital arm, which participated in the biotechnology company’s €20 million (US$21.7 million) seed financing in 2024.

The investment reflected growing pharmaceutical industry interest in antibody-based treatments and the need for better methods of identifying suitable cell surface targets.

The latest agreement builds on AbbVie’s existing investment in bispecific antibody development.

In September 2026, the pharmaceutical company reported improved response rates and progression-free survival in a clinical study of its BCMA x CD3 T-cell engager in patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma.

AbbVie has also pursued external partnerships to expand its pipeline.

In January 2026, it entered into an agreement with China’s RemeGen worth up to US$5.6 billion, covering the development and commercialisation of antibody-based therapies.

Disco builds partnerships in precision oncology

Disco has also partnered with Amgen under a similar collaboration announced earlier in 2026.

The agreement, valued at up to US$618 million, focuses on developing a therapeutic candidate against a target identified by Disco before the partnership.

The growing interest in Disco’s platform reflects a broader shift towards precision oncology, with pharmaceutical companies seeking technologies that can identify more selective targets for antibody-based treatments.

For AbbVie, the collaboration provides access to a platform that could expand its solid tumour research programmes while reducing reliance on conventional single-target approaches.
